THE OWNER'S CONTRACT, verbatim intent: full automation, never skip steps; if a step is not needed, an artifact must say WHY it was skipped, and a process must manage that.

EXTERNAL REVIEW FINDINGS driving this change (Codex verifier, 2026-07-31):
  * "audit_run() reports optional omissions as strings, with no reason, applicability rule, artifact path, hash, timestamp, or authorization. Wiring this function alone would not satisfy the owner's skip-artifact requirement." (episode_dag.py ~line 334)
  * "The graph collapses all four promotion emails into one optional promo_email step and ends at promo_schedule; it contains no distinct warmup, tease, launch, follow-up, referral-ask, referral-follow-up, or public-readback lifecycle steps." (episode_dag.py ~line 108)

THE CHANGE, two parts:

PART 1 — SKIP ARTIFACTS AS FIRST-CLASS OBJECTS.
1. Define SKIP_REASON_CODES, a bounded vocabulary (extendable deliberately, never free-text-only), at minimum: not_applicable, superseded_by, owner_waived, upstream_unavailable, policy_gate. Free text goes in a separate "detail" field; the CODE is what a process can manage.
2. make_skip_artifact(step_id, *, reason_code, detail, authorized_by, now, evidence=None) -> dict
   Returns the canonical skip artifact: {"schema":"episode-skip-v1", "step_id", "reason_code",
   "detail", "authorized_by", "skipped_at" (iso from `now`), "evidence" (list), and
   "content_hash" (sha256 over the sorted canonical JSON of the other fields, so a skip
   artifact cannot be silently edited without the hash changing).
   Raise ValueError on an unknown reason_code, empty authorized_by, or empty detail —
   an unexplained or unowned skip is exactly what the owner has banned.
3. validate_skip_artifact(artifact) -> list[str] of problems; empty means valid. It must
   recompute and check the content_hash. A tampered or schema-less artifact is invalid.
4. audit_run gains a skip_artifacts parameter (mapping step_id -> artifact). Semantics:
   * A required step that did not run and has NO valid skip artifact: run is INCOMPLETE and
     the report names it as a SILENT skip (the banned case).
   * A required step that did not run but has a VALID skip artifact: named in the report as
     an AUTHORIZED skip with its reason_code and authorizer; does not make complete False.
   * An INVALID artifact (bad hash, unknown code) is worse than none: report it as
     "invalid skip artifact" and keep the run incomplete — a forged or corrupted
     authorization must never count.
   * Optional steps unchanged: named, never blocking.

PART 2 — THE DAG COVERS THE FULL LIFECYCLE.
Split and extend the graph so every real external effect is its own step:
  promo_email_warmup, promo_email_tease, promo_email_launch, promo_email_followup
  (replacing the single promo_email step; read the orchestrator's actual unit names —
  publish_units uses promo_email:<stage>:<addr> — and mirror those stages);
  referral_ask (after publish; the system asking the guest for referrals),
  referral_followup (after referral_ask),
  social_schedule (the three-touch week plan, requires certification per the owner's
  schedule-at-certification rule: it must NOT require publish, only certification),
  public_readback (verifying the published artifacts are actually live and consistent;
  requires publish).
Keep guest_assets as a requirement of thumbnail and show_notes (tests already pin this).
Declare requirements honestly from the code you can see; where behaviour is genuinely
policy-gated (emails behind the autonomy ladder), the step exists and a skip artifact with
reason_code policy_gate is the correct representation of "gated today" — encode that in a
test so the pattern is demonstrated.

TESTS (tests/test_skip_artifacts.py; at least 7):
 (1) a required step skipped with NO artifact -> incomplete, named as SILENT;
 (2) the same skip with a VALID artifact (owner_waived, authorized_by set) -> complete,
     named as AUTHORIZED with code and authorizer;
 (3) NEGATIVE: a tampered artifact (mutate detail after creation) fails validate and the
     run stays incomplete, reported as invalid — forged authorization never counts;
 (4) NEGATIVE: make_skip_artifact raises on unknown reason_code, empty detail, empty
     authorized_by;
 (5) the four promo email steps exist as distinct DAG steps matching the orchestrator's
     stage names, and referral_ask/referral_followup/social_schedule/public_readback exist;
 (6) social_schedule requires certification and does NOT require publish;
 (7) a policy_gate skip artifact on promo_email_warmup yields a complete run with the gate
     named — the "gated today" pattern;
 (8) determinism: identical inputs give identical reports.
Keep tests/test_episode_dag.py green; update the E104 replay test if step renames affect it,
with a one-line comment.

OWNED FILES (only these; prep_bridge.py and its test file are new):
  scripts/prep_bridge.py
  scripts/post-prep-sweep-headless.sh
  server/pipeline/post_prep.py
  tests/test_prep_bridge.py

THE DEFECT, measured today. The owner asked why prep-call context never reaches episodes. The pieces all exist and one bridge is missing:
  * scripts/transcribe_daily_prep_recording.py exists and writes raw/prep-call-transcript.txt (see its ~line 157 default output path). Read that script for its exact CLI contract before wiring anything.
  * scripts/prep_sweep_candidates.py (episode_candidates) classifies candidates: reason "transcript_exists_no_followup_sent" when the transcript is already there, reason "s3_event_ready_no_transcript" when the recording landed in S3 but NO transcript exists yet.
  * scripts/post-prep-sweep-headless.sh (~line 77) pipes every candidate straight into `python3 -m server.pipeline.post_prep --prep <dir>` WITHOUT ever invoking the transcriber. So an s3_event_ready_no_transcript candidate reaches post_prep with no transcript.
  * server/pipeline/post_prep.py process_prep_call (~line 395) then does: transcript = "" if the file is missing, and proceeds silently — empty open items, empty prep notes, and nobody is ever told. This is exactly the silent-skip class the owner has banned ("if a step is not needed we still need an artifact saying why it was skipped").

THE FIX, three parts:

1. scripts/prep_bridge.py (new, stdlib only). A small module + CLI that closes the gap:
     ensure_transcript(candidate, *, runner, root) -> dict
   For a candidate dict (shape from prep_sweep_candidates: episode_dir, reason, ...):
     * reason "transcript_exists_no_followup_sent": no transcriber call; return
       {"episode_dir", "action": "already_transcribed"}.
     * reason "s3_event_ready_no_transcript": call runner(episode_dir) — the injected
       callable that actually invokes scripts/transcribe_daily_prep_recording.py — and
       afterwards VERIFY the transcript file now exists and is > 200 bytes. Success:
       {"action": "transcribed", "transcript_path": ...}. Runner raised or file still
       missing/small: {"action": "transcribe_failed", "error": <why>} — recorded, never
       raised out, so one bad recording cannot kill the whole sweep.
     * unknown reason: {"action": "unknown_reason", "error": ...} (fail-closed: it is NOT
       treated as ready).
   main(): reads the candidates JSON from stdin or --candidates-file, processes each with
   a default runner that shells out to the real transcriber (build the exact command from
   the transcriber's own CLI; python3 <abs script> with the episode dir), prints a JSON
   report {"results":[...]} to stdout, exit 0 when every action is in
   {"already_transcribed","transcribed"}, exit 1 otherwise. The report is the receipt.

2. scripts/post-prep-sweep-headless.sh: between the candidates listing and the post_prep
   loop, run the bridge: pipe the candidates JSON through
   `python3 "$REPO/scripts/prep_bridge.py"`, append its JSON report to "$LOG", and only
   feed post_prep the episode dirs whose bridge action is already_transcribed or
   transcribed (a jq-free python3 -c filter is fine, matching the style already used in
   the script). A transcribe_failed candidate is SKIPPED for this sweep with its error in
   the log, and the script's final rc must be nonzero so the existing failure path fires.
   Keep every existing behavior: marker file, preflight, autosend flag, telegram alert.

3. server/pipeline/post_prep.py process_prep_call: when the transcript file is missing or
   empty, do not silently proceed. Keep processing (the prep-summary email flow may still
   be wanted), but record it: add "prep_transcript_missing": True and a short
   "prep_transcript_note" into the returned result dict AND into
   ep._data["prep_call_event"] (persisted via ep.save() on the existing save path), so
   the gap is visible to every downstream consumer instead of masquerading as a quiet
   success. Do not change the email/autosend behavior.

TESTS (tests/test_prep_bridge.py; at least 6, fake runner, tmp dirs):
 (1) THE REAL CASE: an s3_event_ready_no_transcript candidate invokes the runner and,
     with the runner writing a >200-byte transcript, returns action "transcribed";
 (2) a transcript_exists candidate NEVER invokes the runner (assert call count 0);
 (3) NEGATIVE: runner raises -> action transcribe_failed with the error recorded, and
     main()'s exit code is nonzero while OTHER candidates still get processed;
 (4) NEGATIVE: runner succeeds but writes nothing -> transcribe_failed (the bridge trusts
     the artifact, not the runner's word);
 (5) NEGATIVE: unknown reason -> unknown_reason, nonzero exit — fail-closed;
 (6) process_prep_call with no transcript file records prep_transcript_missing=True in
     result and persisted episode data (use the existing test fixtures/fakes in
     tests/test_post_prep.py as the pattern; no real email);
 (7) process_prep_call WITH a transcript does not set the flag.
Keep tests/test_prep_sweep_script.py green.

THE GAP, stated by the owner today: "context in prep and podcast calls being included" is still missing from published episodes. Measured: server/pipeline/show_notes.py generate_show_notes(transcript, guest_bio, ep, kind="publish") (~line 378) builds the PUBLISH notes from the main episode transcript and guest bio only. The prep-call artifacts that already exist on the episode — the prep show notes saved via save_show_notes(..., kind="prep"), the open items in ep._data["prep_call_event"]["open_items"], and raw/prep-call-transcript.txt — are NEVER read when the final notes are written. The guest tells us on the prep call what they want the episode to emphasize, and we throw that away.

THE FIX, inside show_notes.py only:
1. Add a helper gather_prep_context(ep) -> dict returning
   {"prep_notes": <str|None>, "open_items": [...], "prep_transcript_excerpt": <str|None>,
    "sources_used": [names], "missing": [names-with-reason]}.
   Read the prep notes from wherever save_show_notes(kind="prep") puts them (read that
   function; do not guess the path), open items from ep._data, and at most the first ~4000
   characters of the prep transcript. Missing pieces land in "missing" with a reason —
   absence must be legible, never silent.
2. In generate_show_notes when kind is the publish/final kind: include the gathered prep
   context in the generation input (an additional clearly-delimited context block for the
   LLM path, and available to any deterministic path), WITHOUT changing the output
   contract of the notes structure.
3. Record visibility in the returned notes: a "prep_context_used" field listing
   sources_used and "prep_context_missing" listing what was absent and why. Empty prep
   context must yield prep_context_used: [] — a visible statement, not an omission.
4. kind="prep" generation must NOT feed on itself (no recursion into prep context).

TESTS (tests/test_prep_context_in_final_notes.py; at least 5, using the module's existing
fake/seam pattern so no network):
 (1) an episode with prep notes + open items + prep transcript produces publish notes
     whose prep_context_used names all three, and the generation input actually contained
     a distinctive marker string planted in the prep notes (assert the fake saw it);
 (2) NEGATIVE: an episode with NO prep artifacts still generates notes, with
     prep_context_used == [] and prep_context_missing naming each absent source — the
     absence is on the record;
 (3) a >4000-char prep transcript is excerpted, not passed whole;
 (4) kind="prep" generation ignores prep context (no recursion; the fake must NOT see the
     marker);
 (5) NEGATIVE: a corrupt/unreadable prep-notes file is reported in prep_context_missing
     with a reason and does not raise;
 (6) determinism of gather_prep_context given identical inputs.
Keep the three existing show-notes suites green.
